fams.label: Painting
fams.test: a picture made by laying paint or ink on a movable flat support — paper, vellum, panel, canvas, cloth or silk. Wall painting fixed to a building is L.
key: 1. Small-format opaque watercolour or ink on paper or vellum, made for a book or an album? → A1.
2. Ink and colour with the brush on silk or paper in the East Asian formats (hanging scroll, handscroll, screen, album)? → A2.
3. A devotional image on a wooden panel in the icon tradition? → A3. A painting on cloth made to be hung or carried (thangka, pata, phad)? → A4.
4. Oil, tempera or acrylic on canvas or panel in the easel tradition and its modern and contemporary lineages? → A5.
5. A folk or popular painting named as its own tradition (reverse glass, coffeehouse painting, bark painting)? → A6.

subs.label: Manuscript & Album Painting
subs.axis: Axis: the painting tradition (a court and school lineage). Small-format pictures in opaque watercolour or ink on paper or vellum, made to illustrate a book or to be mounted in an album (miniature painting).

leaves.label: Arab Painting
leaves.defn: manuscript painting of the Arab lands from the 12th to the 15th century: illustrated scientific texts, the Maqamat of al-Hariri and Kalila wa Dimna, made in Baghdad, Mosul, Syria and Mamluk Egypt (al-Wasiti's 1237 Maqamat).
leaves.aliases: Arabic miniature; Baghdad school; Mesopotamian school
alias_rows: Yahya ibn Mahmud al-Wasiti → Yahya ibn Mahmoud al-Wasiti

leaves.label: Persian Miniature
leaves.defn: Persian manuscript and album painting from the Mongol conquest to the 19th century, taught in court workshops whose schools are named after their centres (Herat, Tabriz, Qazvin, Isfahan, Shiraz, Bukhara); kinds are those schools and their masters (Bihzad, Sultan Muhammad, Riza-yi 'Abbasi).
leaves.see: A1-3 Ottoman Miniature; A1-4 Mughal Painting; I2-1 Persian Lacquer.

leaves.label: Deccan Painting
leaves.defn: painting of the Deccan sultanates (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda) and of Hyderabad after them, 16th–19th century, with its lyrical colour and Persian, Turkman and Vijayanagara sources.
kinds: Bijapur painter of marbled picture, c.1650; uncertain

leaves.label: Company Painting
leaves.defn: paintings made by Indian artists for officials of the East India Company and other Europeans, 18th–19th century, in a hybrid of Mughal technique and European natural history and topography (Delhi, Lucknow, Patna, Murshidabad, Tanjore).

subs.label: East Asian Ink & Colour Painting
subs.axis: Axis: school and lineage. Built at scale (Chinese, Japanese and Korean painting).

subs.label: Icon Painting
subs.axis: Axis: school. Built at scale (Byzantine, Russian, Ethiopian, Cretan icons).

subs.label: Cloth & Scroll Painting
subs.axis: Axis: tradition. Built at scale (thangka, pata, phad, kalighat).

subs.label: Easel Painting
subs.axis: Axis: period style, school or movement. Built at scale for the European lineage and modern and contemporary painting; the pilot holds one non-European court tradition.

leaves.label: Qajar Painting
leaves.defn: court painting of Qajar Iran (1789–1925) in oil on canvas and in watercolour: life-size royal portraits and figures of pleasure (Mihr 'Ali), and the realist watercolours of Abu'l-Hasan Ghaffari (Sani' al-Mulk).
leaves.see: A1-2 Persian Miniature; I2-1 Persian Lacquer.

fams.label: Drawings & Prints
fams.test: a drawing made as an end in itself or as a design, or an impression pulled from a matrix (woodblock, plate, stone, screen).
key: 1. Drawn by hand? → B1. 2. Printed from a matrix? → B2.

leaves.label: Saz Style
leaves.defn: the Ottoman court style of feathery serrated leaves, rosettes and fabulous creatures drawn in ink by the nakkaşhane under Shahkulu and Kara Memi (16th century), and carried from drawings into tiles, textiles and bindings.
leaves.see: E2-7 Iznik Pottery; H3-3 Ottoman Silk Textiles.

subs.label: Printmaking
subs.axis: Axis: process, then school. Built at scale (ukiyo-e, chiaroscuro woodcut, etching).

fams.label: Book Arts & Calligraphy
fams.test: the written or decorated book or page is the work: calligraphy, illumination (ornament), binding and paper decoration, or a manuscript tradition studied as the book.
key: 1. Writing as an art, judged by its script? → C1 (placed by script family).
2. A manuscript tradition or its illumination (ornament, frontispieces, headings, borders)? → C2.
3. The binding? → C3. Decorated paper (marbling, paper cutting)? → C4.

subs.label: Calligraphy
subs.axis: Axis: script family and its lineage of masters.

leaves.label: Kufic
leaves.defn: the angular early Arabic script of Qur'ans on parchment and of inscriptions, with its later Eastern (broken cursive), floriated, plaited and square (banna'i) forms.

leaves.label: Maghribi Script
leaves.defn: the rounded scripts of al-Andalus, North Africa and West Africa (mabsut, mujawhar, Andalusi, Sudani), written with a pointed pen.

leaves.label: Six Pens (al-Aqlam al-Sitta)
leaves.defn: the proportioned cursive scripts — thuluth, naskh, muhaqqaq, rayhani, tawqi' and riqa' — codified by Ibn Muqla and Ibn al-Bawwab and perfected by Yaqut al-Musta'simi, then carried by his pupils and by the Ottoman masters (Sheikh Hamdullah, Hafiz Osman).

leaves.label: Sini
leaves.defn: Chinese Arabic calligraphy, written with a brush in a rounded style on scrolls and Qur'ans of the Hui Muslims.

leaves.label: Early Qur'anic Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Qur'ans written on parchment in Hijazi and Kufic scripts from the 7th to the 10th century, in horizontal format with sparse illuminated headings (the Blue Qur'an, the Tübingen and Birmingham fragments).
leaves.aliases: early Qur'ans; Hijazi Qur'ans; Kufic Qur'ans

leaves.label: Islamic Illumination
leaves.defn: the illumination of Qur'ans and books after about 1000: gilded and painted frontispieces, sura headings, margins and borders, in the Abbasid, Mamluk, Ilkhanid, Timurid and Safavid (tazhib), Ottoman (tezhip) and Mughal traditions, with its named illuminators.

leaves.label: Timbuktu Manuscripts
leaves.defn: the manuscripts of the West African Islamic scholarly tradition (Timbuktu, Djenné, the Sahel), in Arabic and in Ajami (African languages in Arabic script), with their Sudani script and leather satchel bindings.
gathered: West African Ajami / Sahelian Islamic (see islamic_world.py) (manuscripts)

leaves.label: Malay Manuscripts
leaves.defn: illuminated Malay manuscripts in Jawi script from the Islamic sultanates of the Malay world (Aceh, Terengganu, Java), with their floral frontispieces.

leaves.label: Islamic Bookbinding
leaves.defn: the bindings of the Islamic book: tooled, stamped and filigree-cut leather with the envelope flap, and from the 15th century painted lacquer bindings.

leaves.label: Ebru
leaves.defn: paper marbling as practised in Ottoman Turkey and Iran: colours floated on size and transferred to paper, used for album margins and endpapers.

fams.label: Sculpture & Carving
fams.test: carved, modelled or cast in three dimensions as an image or as carving for its own sake: statues, reliefs, carved stucco and stone ornament, ivory, bone, jade, rock crystal and hardstone, masks and puppets.
key: 1. Carved stucco, stone or terracotta ornament from buildings? → D1. 2. Ivory or bone? → D2. 3. Rock crystal, jade or other hardstone? → D3.
4. A mask or puppet made for performance? → D4. 5. Figurative sculpture in stone, wood, metal or clay? → D5.

leaves.label: Samarra Stucco
leaves.defn: the carved and moulded stucco of the Abbasid capital Samarra (9th century) in its three styles, of which the third, the bevelled style, carried abstract ornament across the early Islamic world.

leaves.label: Nasrid Stucco (Yesería)
leaves.defn: the carved and painted stucco of Nasrid Granada and the Mudéjar workshops (Alhambra wall panels, muqarnas).

leaves.label: Andalusian Ivories
leaves.defn: carved ivory boxes and pyxides of the Umayyad caliphal workshops of Córdoba and Madinat al-Zahra and of the taifa courts (10th–11th century).
src: Wikidata Q2864629 (art of the Umayyads of Cordoba)
alias_rows: ‘Abd al-Rahman bin Zaywan → 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayyan

leaves.label: Siculo-Arabic Ivories
leaves.defn: painted and gilded ivory caskets made in Norman Sicily and southern Italy (12th–13th century) in an Arabic decorative idiom.

leaves.label: Fatimid Rock Crystal
leaves.defn: vessels and objects carved from rock crystal in Fatimid Egypt (10th–11th century), above all the ewers with relief decoration later mounted in European church treasuries.

leaves.label: Mughal Jade
leaves.defn: jade and hardstone vessels carved for the Timurid and Mughal courts, culminating in Shah Jahan's wine cup (1657).
src: Wikidata Q17053650 (Wine cup of Shah Jahan)
kinds: Jahangir's jade cup maker, court goldsmith

leaves.label: Karagöz Shadow Puppets
leaves.defn: the translucent painted leather puppets of the Ottoman shadow theatre of Karagöz and Hacivat.

subs.label: Figurative Sculpture
subs.axis: Axis: period style, school or movement. Built at scale.

fams.label: Ceramics
fams.test: made of fired clay: pottery, tiles and ceramic objects, placed by their body (fabric) and then their named ware.
key: 1. Earthenware body (porous, fired low), whether unglazed, slip-decorated, lead-glazed, tin-glazed or lustred? → E1.
2. Fritware (stonepaste: ground quartz, glass frit and a little clay)? → E2.
3. Stoneware? → E3. 4. Porcelain? → E4.
Then the named ware; lustre and tin-glaze are techniques inside a body, not sub-families (P4).

subs.label: Earthenware
subs.axis: Axis: named ware (decoration technique and centre).

leaves.label: Abbasid Tin-Glazed Ware
leaves.defn: earthenware with an opaque white tin glaze made in Basra and southern Iraq from the 9th century in imitation of Chinese porcelain, painted in cobalt blue and green (Abbasid blue-and-white).
leaves.aliases: opaque white ware; Basra ware; Abbasid blue-and-white
kinds: Abbasid potter, signed bowl, 9th c.; uncertain

leaves.label: Abbasid Lustreware
leaves.defn: the first lustre pottery: tin-glazed earthenware painted in metallic lustre in 9th–10th-century Iraq, polychrome then monochrome, exported as far as Samarra and Kairouan.
leaves.see: E1-3 Fatimid Lustreware; E2-2 Kashan Lustreware.
kinds: Basra potter, signed dish, 9th c.; uncertain

leaves.label: Fatimid Lustreware
leaves.defn: lustre-painted earthenware of Fatimid Egypt (10th–12th century), often figural, signed by potters such as Muslim ibn al-Dahhan and Sa'd.
kinds: Sa'd, Fatimid lustre potter; tentative attribution, uncertain

leaves.label: Samanid Slipware
leaves.defn: earthenware of Nishapur and Samarqand (9th–10th century) painted in coloured slips under a clear glaze, above all the epigraphic ware with Arabic aphorisms on a white ground.
leaves.aliases: Nishapur ware; epigraphic slipware; Samanid epigraphic ware

leaves.label: Splashware
leaves.defn: earthenware splashed with green, yellow and brown glazes in imitation of Chinese sancai, made in Iraq and Iran from the 9th century.

leaves.label: Persian Sgraffito Ware
leaves.defn: slip-covered earthenware incised through the slip and glazed, made in Iran and the Caucasus from the 10th to the 13th century (Garrus, Aghkand and Amol wares).
leaves.aliases: Garrus ware; Aghkand ware; Amol ware; sgraffito

leaves.label: Islamic Unglazed Pottery
leaves.defn: unglazed earthenware with carved, moulded, stamped or barbotine decoration, above all the pierced filters of water jugs (Egypt, Syria, Iraq, 10th–14th century).
kinds: early Abbasid potter, signed jar, 8th c.; uncertain

leaves.label: Hispano-Moresque Ware
leaves.defn: tin-glazed and lustred earthenware of Islamic and Christian Spain (Málaga, Manises, Paterna, Valencia), 13th–16th century, carried to Italy as the model of maiolica.
leaves.aliases: Valencian lustreware; Manises ware; Málaga ware

leaves.label: Çanakkale Pottery
leaves.defn: the boldly modelled and splash-painted earthenware of Çanakkale on the Dardanelles (17th–19th century).

leaves.label: Fez Pottery
leaves.defn: the urban and rural earthenware of Morocco: the blue-and-polychrome tin-glazed wares of Fez, the pottery of Safi and the green glazed ware of Tamegroute.
leaves.aliases: Fassi pottery; Moroccan pottery; Safi pottery; Tamegroute pottery
leaves.weak: no English source names 'Moroccan pottery' as one tradition; 'poterie de Fès / de Safi' in French sources

leaves.label: Kabyle Pottery
leaves.defn: hand-built earthenware painted in red and black slips by Kabyle women potters of northern Algeria.

leaves.label: Sejnane Pottery
leaves.defn: hand-modelled earthenware of the women of Sejnane in northern Tunisia, inscribed by UNESCO in 2018.
leaves.aliases: pottery skills of the women of Sejnane

leaves.label: Rishton Ceramics
leaves.defn: the blue-glazed (ishkor) earthenware of Rishtan and the centres of the Fergana Valley and Bukhara oasis (Gijduvan) in Uzbekistan.

leaves.label: Seljuk Pottery
leaves.defn: fritware of Seljuq Iran and its neighbours (11th–13th century) other than its named lustre, mina'i and lajvardina wares: monochrome and carved, silhouette, laqabi and underglaze-painted wares.
leaves.aliases: Seljuq pottery; monochrome ware; silhouette ware; laqabi ware
leaves.see: E2-2 Kashan Lustreware; E2-3 Mina'i Ware.

leaves.label: Kashan Lustreware
leaves.defn: lustre-painted fritware of Kashan (late 12th–14th century) — vessels and the star, cross and mihrab tiles of Iranian shrines — signed by potter families such as Abu Tahir and Abu Zayd.
leaves.see: E1-2 Abbasid Lustreware; E2-3 Mina'i Ware.
kinds: Abu Zayd, Persian, active late 12th–early 13th century
Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Tahir
Abū Zayd ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Zayd

leaves.label: Mina'i Ware
leaves.defn: overglaze-painted fritware of Kashan (late 12th–early 13th century), with figural scenes in seven colours.

leaves.label: Lajvardina
leaves.defn: Ilkhanid fritware with a cobalt-blue (lajvard) or turquoise glaze overpainted in white, red and gold leaf (late 13th–14th century).

leaves.label: Raqqa Ware
leaves.defn: fritware of Raqqa and Syria (12th–13th century), lustred or underglaze-painted in black under a turquoise glaze.

leaves.label: Sultanabad Ware
leaves.defn: Ilkhanid fritware of the late 13th–14th century with a grey-green slip and Chinese-inspired lotus and animal designs.

leaves.label: Iznik Pottery
leaves.defn: the fritware of Iznik in Ottoman Anatolia (late 15th–17th century) — vessels and tiles in its successive styles: blue-and-white (Abraham of Kütahya), Golden Horn, Damascus and Rhodian with its bole red.

leaves.label: Damascus Tiles
leaves.defn: Ottoman-period fritware and tiles made in Damascus (16th–17th century), painted in blues, green and manganese without Iznik's red.

leaves.label: Kubachi Ware
leaves.defn: Safavid fritware of north-western Iran (16th–17th century) with crackled glaze, found in the village of Kubachi in Daghestan.

leaves.label: Safavid Pottery
leaves.defn: the fritware of Safavid Iran (16th–17th century) other than Kubachi ware: Kirman and Mashhad blue-and-white in the manner of Chinese porcelain, celadon imitations and late lustre.
leaves.aliases: Kirman ware; Persian blue-and-white; Gombroon ware

leaves.label: Kütahya Ceramics
leaves.defn: the fritware of Kütahya in western Anatolia (18th–19th century), small vessels and tiles often made by Armenian potters for church and household.
leaves.see: E2-7 Iznik Pottery; E1-9 Çanakkale Pottery.

leaves.label: Qajar Ceramics
leaves.defn: the tiles and vessels of Qajar Iran (19th century): moulded and painted figural tiles of Tehran and Shiraz (Ali Muhammad Isfahani) and revival lustre.

leaves.label: Qallaline Tiles
leaves.defn: the tin-glazed tiles of the Qallaline quarter of Tunis (17th–19th century), with Ottoman and Italian floral designs.
kinds: The craftsman may have been the Tunisian, al-Hajj Mas’ud al-Sab’a

fams.label: Glass
fams.test: made of glass, placed by how it is formed and decorated.
key: 1. Decorated by cutting or carving? → F2. 2. Painted with enamel or gilding? → F3. 3. Lustre-painted? → F4. 4. Window or stained glass? → F5. 5. Otherwise blown or moulded glass → F1.

leaves.label: Beykoz Glass
leaves.defn: Ottoman glass of the Beykoz and Istanbul workshops (late 18th–19th century), above all the çeşm-i bülbül ('nightingale's eye') ware with spiral white and coloured threads.

leaves.label: Syrian Glassblowing
leaves.defn: the free-blown glass of the Damascus and Hebron workshops, inscribed by UNESCO in 2023 as a heritage in need of urgent safeguarding.

leaves.label: Islamic Cut Glass
leaves.defn: glass decorated by wheel-cutting and relief-carving in Iran, Iraq and Egypt (9th–11th century), from facet-cut bowls to relief-cut cameo glass and the Hedwig glasses.

leaves.label: Mamluk Enamelled Glass
leaves.defn: enamelled and gilded glass of Ayyubid and Mamluk Syria and Egypt (13th–14th century): mosque lamps, beakers and bottles with blazons and inscriptions.

leaves.label: Islamic Lustre-Painted Glass
leaves.defn: glass stained with metallic lustre in Egypt, Syria and Iraq (8th–11th century), the predecessor of lustre pottery.

fams.label: Metalwork, Arms & Jewellery
fams.test: made of metal: vessels and objects, instruments, arms and armour, and jewellery.
key: 1. Worn as ornament? → G3. 2. A weapon or armour? → G2. 3. Otherwise vessels, objects and instruments of base or precious metal, cast, raised, engraved or inlaid → G1.

subs.label: Metalwork
subs.axis: Axis: workshop tradition (named school or technique).

leaves.label: Khurasan Metalwork
leaves.defn: cast and inlaid brass of eastern Iran and Herat (12th–13th century), with silver and copper inlay and figural bands (the Bobrinsky Bucket, 1163).

leaves.label: Mosul School of Metalwork
leaves.defn: inlaid brass made by craftsmen with the nisba al-Mawsili in Mosul, Syria and Egypt (13th century), the model for Ayyubid and Mamluk inlay.

leaves.label: Ottoman Tombak
leaves.defn: fire-gilded copper of the Ottoman court (17th–19th century): ewers, basins, censers and mosque fittings.

leaves.label: Bidri Ware
leaves.defn: zinc-alloy objects inlaid with silver and blackened, from Bidar in the Deccan (from the 14th century).

leaves.label: Koftgari
leaves.defn: damascening of steel with gold and silver wire, practised in Mughal and Rajput India and in Iran for arms and objects.

leaves.label: Islamic Astrolabes
leaves.defn: brass astrolabes and celestial globes of the Islamic world, engraved instruments made by named makers in Baghdad, Isfahan, Lahore and al-Andalus.

leaves.label: Firoozeh Koobi
leaves.defn: Iranian metal objects set with turquoise chips in a mosaic over the surface (Isfahan, Mashhad).

leaves.label: Persian Metalwork
leaves.defn: inlaid and engraved brass and steel of Iran after the Mongols: Inju Fars inlay (14th century), Timurid and Safavid tinned-brass jugs, candlesticks and inkwells with poetic inscriptions, and Qajar cut steel (Hajji 'Abbas).
leaves.aliases: Timurid metalwork; Safavid metalwork; Qajar steel
leaves.weak: attested as a period group (Timurid, Safavid metalwork) in museum essays; no item for the umbrella name

leaves.label: Islamic Arms and Armour
leaves.defn: the arms and armour of the Islamic courts: Mamluk and Ottoman helmets and mail, Persian shamshirs and watered-steel (wootz) blades, Ottoman yatağans and Mughal talwars, katars and jade-hilted daggers.

leaves.label: Fatimid Jewellery
leaves.defn: gold jewellery of Fatimid Egypt and Syria (10th–12th century) in filigree and granulation, often enamelled.

leaves.label: Mughal Jewellery
leaves.defn: jewellery and jewelled objects of the Mughal court: kundan setting, enamelled (minakari) backs, carved emeralds and jade inlaid with gems.

leaves.label: Bedouin Jewellery
leaves.defn: the silver jewellery of the Bedouin and settled peoples of Arabia, Yemen and Oman, worked in filigree, granulation and with coral and carnelian.

leaves.label: Berber Jewellery
leaves.defn: the silver jewellery of the Amazigh peoples of Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia: fibulae, headdresses and the cloisonné enamel of Kabylia.

fams.label: Textiles, Carpets & Dress
fams.test: made of fibre: carpets and rugs, woven, embroidered, dyed and felted textiles, and dress.

subs.label: Pile Carpets & Rugs

leaves.label: Persian Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted-pile carpets of Iran, from the Safavid court carpets (the Ardabil carpet, hunting and vase carpets, Polonaise carpets) to the city, village and tribal rugs named by their centres and peoples (Tabriz, Kashan, Isfahan, Kerman, Heriz, Qashqai, Bakhtiari).

leaves.label: Anatolian Rug
leaves.defn: knotted-pile carpets of Anatolia from the Seljuq Konya carpets onward: animal carpets, the 'Holbein' and 'Lotto' carpets known from European paintings, Ushak star and medallion carpets, and the village rugs of Bergama, Konya and Ghiordes.

leaves.label: Mamluk Carpet
leaves.defn: carpets woven in Cairo under the Mamluks (late 15th–early 16th century) in red, green and blue with kaleidoscopic geometric fields.

leaves.label: Caucasian Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted-pile rugs of the Caucasus — Kazak, Karabagh, Shirvan, Kuba and the dragon carpets — and of the Azerbaijani schools.

leaves.label: Turkmen Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted-pile carpets and tent furnishings of the Turkmen tribes (Tekke, Yomut, Salor, Saryk, Ersari), with their tribal güls.

leaves.label: Baluch Rug

leaves.label: Afghan Rug
leaves.defn: knotted rugs of Afghanistan, including the war rugs woven since 1979 with weapons and maps.

leaves.label: Mughal Carpet
leaves.defn: knotted carpets of the Mughal workshops of Lahore, Agra and Kashmir (late 16th–17th century): pictorial and flowering-plant carpets of very fine weave.

leaves.label: Moroccan Rug
leaves.defn: the pile and flatwoven rugs of the Amazigh tribes of Morocco (Beni Ouarain, Azilal, Boucherouite) and of the urban workshops of Rabat.

leaves.label: Kilim
leaves.defn: tapestry-woven flatweaves of Anatolia, Iran, the Caucasus, Central Asia and North Africa, from slit-tapestry Anatolian kilims to Persian gelims, gabbeh-like tribal weaves and Tunisian mergoum.

leaves.label: Soumak
leaves.defn: weft-wrapped flatweaves of the Caucasus and north-west Iran, with a herringbone surface.

leaves.label: Al Sadu
leaves.defn: the warp-faced weaving of the Bedouin of Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Qatar, for tents and camel trappings (UNESCO 2011).

leaves.label: Tiraz
leaves.defn: inscribed textiles from the caliphal workshops (tiraz) of the Umayyads, Abbasids and Fatimids, with bands of embroidered or tapestry-woven Arabic inscriptions.

leaves.label: Safavid Silk Textiles
leaves.defn: the figured silks, lampas, brocades and velvets of Safavid Iran (Ghiyath al-Din 'Ali-yi Naqshband), with figural scenes and floral fields.

leaves.label: Ottoman Silk Textiles

leaves.label: Oya

leaves.label: Khayamiya
leaves.defn: the appliqué tent panels of the Cairo tentmakers' street, Sharia al-Khayamiya.

leaves.label: Balochi Needlework

fams.label: New Media, Installation & Performance
fams.test: time-based, installed or performed work: video, sound, installation, performance, digital and net art. Built at scale (artist-led).

familyKey: 1. Is it a building or a designed built whole (a garden, a complex), placed by its style? → K Architecture. Ornament carved, painted or tiled on a building and studied where it stands is asked next (2); loose architectural fragments in a museum go by their material (D, E, I).
2. Is it made on or into a fixed surface and studied where it stands: rock art, wall painting, in-situ mosaic and tile revetment, a geoglyph, or art on the living body? → L Art in Place.
3. Is it a photograph or made with a camera? → J Photography. Is it time-based, installed or performed (video, installation, performance, digital)? → M New Media, Installation & Performance.

4. Is the written or decorated book the work: calligraphy, illumination (ornament), binding, paper decoration, or a manuscript tradition studied as the book? → C Book Arts & Calligraphy. Pictures in a manuscript belong to a painting tradition and go on to 6 (precedence P1).
5. Is it a drawing made as an end in itself or as a design, or a print pulled from a matrix? → B Drawings & Prints.
6. Is it a picture made with paint or ink on a movable flat support (paper, vellum, panel, canvas, cloth, silk)? → A Painting.

7. Is it carved, modelled or cast as an image or as carving for its own sake: statues, reliefs, carved stucco, ivory, bone, jade, rock crystal and hardstone, masks and puppets? → D Sculpture & Carving. A vessel carved from rock crystal or jade stays here; a cast metal vessel is G.

8. Otherwise place it by its material: fired clay → E Ceramics; glass → F Glass; metal (vessels, instruments, arms, jewellery) → G Metalwork, Arms & Jewellery; fibre (carpets, woven, embroidered, dyed and felted textiles, dress) → H Textiles, Carpets & Dress; wood, lacquer and papier-mâché, furniture → I Woodwork, Lacquer & Furniture.
Inside a family, run the family's own key (on each family card), then choose the leaf whose definition fits; a leaf's kinds are its named sub-schools, centres, workshops, sub-types and makers.
precedence: Pictures painted in a manuscript or for an album go to A1 Manuscript & Album Painting when the tradition is studied as painting (Persian, Ottoman, Mughal, Deccan, Arab); the book as an object — its script, illumination ornament and binding — goes to C. An illustrated manuscript is placed by what makes it notable: its pictures → A1, its script or illumination → C.

A tile is placed by its ware in E Ceramics (Iznik tiles under Iznik Pottery; Kashan lustre tiles under Kashan Lustreware). A revetment assembled on site as a named technique — cut-tile mosaic, zellige, kashi kari, mirror mosaic — is L3, because the work is the wall.

Carved stucco, stone and wood that survive as museum fragments go to their material family (D1 carving, I1 woodwork). The building that carries them is K; a named in-situ programme of painting or mosaic is L.
Lustre is a surface technique, not a sub-family: a lustreware is placed by its body (earthenware lustre → E1; fritware lustre → E2) and then by its named ware.
A vessel carved from rock crystal, jade or other hardstone is D3 (the carving is the work), not glass or metalwork, even when mounted in metal.

A dynasty, reign, empire or period (Mamluk, Safavid, Qajar, Akbar's reign) is a period tag, never a node. The node is the tradition the work belongs to in its medium: Mamluk enamelled glass (F3), Mamluk metalwork (G1), Mamluk carpets (H1), Mamluk architecture (K).

A city, production centre, country or culture label (Iznik, Kashan, Tabriz, 'Iranian', 'Syrian') is a place tag. A centre becomes a kind under a leaf only when the field names a distinct school or ware after it (Herat school, Kashan lustreware, Ushak carpets).

A revival built outside the original tradition (Moorish Revival synagogues, Neo-Mamluk, the First National Architectural Movement) is a leaf in K Historicist & National Revivals, never a kind of the style it revives.

A named maker is a kind under the leaf of the tradition they worked in, linked to their school or atelier where one is recorded. A maker active in two traditions is placed where most of their recorded work sits, with a see-also to the other (Mir Sayyid Ali and Abd al-Samad: Persian schooling, Mughal atelier → Mughal Painting).

A folk or vernacular craft that the field names on its own (suzani, kilim, Berber jewellery) is its own leaf in the medium family; a court or urban tradition of the same medium is a separate leaf. Garment types (abaya, shemagh, ghutra) are not art traditions: they belong to the Possession Taxonomy.
modifiers: Period and dynasty — a filter on every kind and leaf (Umayyad, Abbasid, Fatimid, Seljuq, Ilkhanid, Mamluk, Timurid, Safavid, Ottoman, Mughal, Qajar ...). Never a node (P6).
Region and place — the 20-region grid of the gathering, plus production centre and country as tags (P7).

Ornament and motif — girih (geometric strapwork), arabesque (islimi), muqarnas, saz leaves, cintamani: a tag across media, never a leaf, since one motif runs through tiles, carpets, metalwork and buildings (open question Q6).
Holding institution and collection — evidence, never a node.
Patron and reign — a tag (Akbar, Shah Tahmasp, Süleyman); a royal atelier is a kind only when it is a recorded workshop (Imperial Mughal atelier, the Ottoman nakkaşhane).

Object type — bowl, ewer, tile, folio, page: an attribute of representative works, not a node. A leaf is a tradition, not an object type, except where the field treats the type as a tradition (astrolabes).
Inscription and script on objects — an attribute; calligraphy as an art (C1) is placed by script.

fams.label: Feature Film
fams.test: a film of 40 minutes or more made as a single work for cinema, festival, television or streaming release; not anime.
key: 1. Non-fiction? → A13 Documentary.

2. Does it belong to a named genre cycle (the narrower leaves of A2–A12: chanbara, kaidan, J-horror, yakuza, noir, pink, Roman Porno, pinky violence, kaiju, tokusatsu, Taiyōzoku)? → skip to that leaf (F1). Otherwise, is it an attested member of a named film movement? → A1 Movements & Schools.

3. Is erotic display or sexual obsession the film's reason to exist — made for the sex-film circuit, or an art-house film built on it? → A12 Erotic Film. A violent exploitation cycle with erotic elements (pinky violence) is not: it goes on.
4. Does it aim first to frighten (ghosts, monsters, killers, gore)? → A4 Horror (F3).
5. Is its premise speculative science — the future, technology, space, giant monsters, transforming heroes? → A5 Science Fiction & Monster (F5). Magic or myth? → A6 Fantasy & Adventure.
6. Is it set in a past era that defines it, or about war? → A7 Historical, Period & War (F4). A frontier western → A17 Western.
7. Criminals or police at the centre? → A2 Crime. Suspense, conspiracy or puzzle? → A3 Thriller & Mystery (F6).
8. Fights, chases and stunts carry it? → A8 Action & Martial Arts.
9. Songs carry the story? → A11 Musical & Music. Laughter first? → A10 Comedy. A love story? → A9 Romance. Otherwise → A14 Drama (F7).

familyKey: 1. Is it Japanese animation (anime), in any format — TV series, film, OVA, ONA, special? → E Anime; format is a filter (D4). Animation from elsewhere is placed by its form below (a feature → A15 Animated Feature).
2. Is it an unscripted format licensed across countries (talent competition, dating, cooking, game show, docusoap)? → G Unscripted Formats.
3. Is it a long-running serial in a named serial tradition — telenovela, dizi, Indian daily soap, soap opera? → D Serial Drama Traditions.

4. Any other scripted series or miniseries, from anywhere — including the East and Southeast Asian drama traditions (K-drama, Chinese costume drama, asadora, taiga drama, lakorn)? → C Television Series (D3: Asian drama is a filter, not a family).
5. A film under 40 minutes? → B Short Film. Otherwise → A Feature Film (the Academy's 40-minute line).
precedence: A film with a home in a named genre cycle (chanbara, kaidan, J-horror, yakuza, film noir, pink film, Roman Porno, pinky violence, kaiju, tokusatsu, Taiyōzoku) goes to that cycle, even when a movement's reference sources list it as a member. A movement leaf keeps the attested members with no cycle home; every attested member carries the movement as a tag (D1).
A named cycle with its own canon (J-horror, kaiju eiga, yakuza eiga, pink film) beats the general genre leaf (supernatural horror, monster film, gangster film, sexploitation).
A film whose story turns on ghosts or the supernatural is horror (kaidan eiga) even when set in the Edo period; period setting alone does not make jidaigeki win.
A jidaigeki whose drama is carried by sword combat is chanbara; a period film of manners, politics or family is jidaigeki.
A film built on a giant monster (kaiju) is Kaiju Film whether or not a costumed hero appears; a costumed transforming hero with no giant monster at its centre is Tokusatsu Hero Film.
Criminals or police and their world at the centre → Crime; suspense built on a threat to an ordinary protagonist, a conspiracy or a puzzle → Thriller & Mystery.
A love story as the main line → Romance; aimed at laughter first → Comedy; otherwise Drama, divided by its subject.

A fantastical or science-fiction device that only frames a love story or a youth drama (a time slip, a letter from the future) does not make the film fantasy or science fiction: it is placed by the story it frames (A9, A14-3).
When a film named as a leaf example would be sent elsewhere by the key, the key wins and the example is replaced; examples never override the key.
Japanese animation is always E Anime, never an animated-feature leaf, whatever list it was selected from.
modifiers: Country of origin — a filter (Wikidata P495 first, as in the selection rule; a co-production counts in each of its countries, D8). National cinemas are never divisions; national cycles and movements defined by what the films are (J-horror, Japanese New Wave) are leaves.
Decade and period of release — a filter.
Director, studio, writer — tags; studio-branded cycles are leaves only where the field names them as a genre (Nikkatsu Roman Porno).
Setting — jidaigeki (pre-1868) or gendaigeki (contemporary) as a filter on every Japanese film; a leaf (Jidaigeki) exists only for the period drama genre.
Release format — theatrical, V-cinema (direct-to-video), TV movie, streaming: a filter.
Movement — a tag on every attested member of a named movement (Japanese New Wave), including members placed in a genre cycle (D1).
Format — for anime: TV series, film, OVA, ONA, special (D4). For series: miniseries, limited, ongoing.
Asian drama — the drama database's scope (Korea, China, Japan, Taiwan, Thailand, the Philippines, Hong Kong, Singapore) as a filter on Television Series (D3).
Source material (manga, novel, true story) — a tag.
Audience counts (Letterboxd, IMDb, MAL, MDL) — kept internal (licensing); never shown.

Gap closed on the way: MDBList returns TMDB keywords (append keyword) and the TMDB plot overview in its batch endpoint. They are now fetched for every selected film (18,268 of 18,365 have keywords) and scripted series (6,870 of 7,134), with Wikidata genre, director and movement facts for the pilot titles. The Wikipedia API stays rate-limited from this machine; it was not needed.

Audits

Blind placement test

A fresh rater saw only the keys and leaf definitions. Visual Art: 39 of 50 held-out items got the same home. Film: 29 of 40 films got the same leaf. What it showed and what changed:

  • Five Visual Art misses were one naming fault: school kinds carried the sweep's "dynasty + city" labels (Timurid Herat), which the rater took for tags. They now carry the field's names (Herat school, Qazvin school, Baghdad school, Inju school).
  • Makers active in two media (illuminator or painter, saz designer or painter) and credit lines naming a scribe and an illuminator split between C1, C2 and A1. Rule P9 (most recorded work wins) stands; the credit-line rows need a parser that splits the names.
  • Film misses sat on four seams: body horror vs cyberpunk (Tetsuo II), manga action vs chanbara (Rurouni Kenshin), psychological horror vs character study (Kotoko, Helter Skelter), crime vs comedy (Why Don't You Play in Hell?), plus Q1.

Seam audit

Leaf pairs that most often appear as primary and see-also in the film placements: Social Drama / Character Study (8), Coming-of-Age / Romantic Drama (8), Crime Drama / Psychological Thriller (6), Shomingeki / Family Drama (5), Jidaigeki / Social Drama (5), Superhero & Manga Action / Chanbara (5). Fixes made: F9 (a fantastical device that only frames a love or youth story does not make it fantasy), F10 (the key wins over a leaf's own examples), key step 3 now covers art-house erotic dramas, and Historical Drama now takes fictional Meiji–Shōwa stories.

Coverage probes

A second rater wrote 75 probes from memory before reading the leaves — core terms a reference must cover and naive phrasings ("Persian rug", "samurai movie"). 61 found a good home. Added from the misses: Javanese Mosque Architecture, Taiyōzoku Film, Atomic Bomb Film; ornament, setting (jidaigeki/gendaigeki) and release format (V-cinema) became tags. Added from the placement review before that: Persian Metalwork, Islamic Woodwork, ʿAjami, Edirnekâri, Qallaline Tiles, Al-Qatt Al-Asiri, Indo-Saracenic Architecture, Slasher Film, Psychological Horror, Pinky Violence, Animal Film and a Western sub-family.

Gathering gap found by the probes: Imamura's Black Rain (1989; 7,233 Letterboxd ratings) is not in the film selection: the 5% top-up for Japan in the 1980s did not reach it. The atomic-bomb leaf is empty for that reason. Japanese 1980s films need a second look in the film top-up.

Attestation

Every leaf shows its source on its card: a Wikidata item (QID, sitelinks) and its Wikipedia article where one exists, otherwise a museum or encyclopedia page found by targeted search. Labels were renamed to the attested form where the search found one (Veneto-Saracenic, Kütahya Ceramics, Damascus Tiles, Moʿaraq, Rishton). Leaves whose name is still weakly attested in English carry a yellow note: Fez Pottery, Ottoman Mother-of-Pearl Inlay, Persian Metalwork, Islamic Woodwork, Edirnekâri, Javanese Mosque Architecture. Six false Wikidata matches were caught and blocked (Illumination → a film company, Kashi → an ancient kingdom).

How the placements were made

  • Rules first. Tradition labels from the sweeps were mapped by hand to leaves, kinds, aliases or tags (pipelines/classify/pilot_islamic.py); 845 of 1,357 rows were placed this way.
  • Makers reviewed one by one. All 668 named makers were reviewed in three batches against the leaf list: spelling variants merged (Basavana → Basawan), regex errors corrected (Bihzad and the Timurid calligraphers had been filed under the Mughal atelier), and non-makers excluded. Kalan/Khord pairs stay separate painters.
  • Films placed with features. Each Japanese film was placed by running the key with its TMDB keywords, overview, Wikidata genre and director, and the film's own history; New Wave membership needed the reference list.
  • Everything is reproducible: python3 pipelines/classify/build_pilot.py merges the rules, the reviewed files in taxonomy/pilot/review/ and the overrides in seeds/classify/, and writes the placements, the census and this page's data.

Open items from the brief

  • Aboriginal artists (ethnic group P172 or art-centre links), Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi and the long-running-serial node, Korean anime top-up, Difret: outside the two pilot slices; they are scheduled with the Oceania, serial-drama, anime and African-film builds.
  • Known noise met in this slice and handled: literati and statesmen among pre-1400 "calligraphers" (Raja ibn Haywa, Ibn ʿAttash excluded), Wikidata trades and garment types in the folk sweep, the 260 unmapped in-situ items, fallback "kind – country" mural buckets.
  • Anime-film matching: 203 of the 301 Japanese animated films in the film selection were matched to the anime selection by title and year; the rest differ only in romanisation and are matched in the anime build, so each keeps one home.

Scaling plan after your review

  1. Rulings D1–D8 are applied and the blind test re-run (above).
  2. Visual Art, tradition-led cells region by region (South Asia, East Asian ceramics and sculpture, Africa, the Americas, Oceania, the ancient world), with kinds seeded from the object records.
  3. Visual Art, artist-led cells: period styles and movements as leaves (Europe 1400–1900, modern, contemporary); artists with no attested movement need a rule (proposal: the period-style leaf of their medium).
  4. Film & Television: the remaining 17,600 films by the same key (features now carry keywords), then scripted TV, serial traditions, anime, Asian drama and unscripted formats.
  5. Full audit (blind test, seams, probes, census) per tab, then the first full release with frozen codes.
